questions.question: What are the three minimum files in the minimal agent workbench?
options: README.md, requirements.txt, main.py
AGENTS.md (router), agent_state.json (system of record), task_board.json (queue)
config.yaml, tasks.json, memory.json
instructions.md, progress.json, backlog.csv
questions.explanation: The three minimum files: AGENTS.md (a short router pointing to deeper docs and files), agent_state.json (the system of record tracking current task, touched files, assumptions, next action), and task_board.json (the work queue with status: todo/in_progress/done/blocked).

questions.question: Why should AGENTS.md be short and act as a router rather than a long manual?
options: Short files load faster
Long manuals get ignored; short routers get followed — they point to deeper docs loaded only when needed
AGENTS.md has a character limit
Short files are easier to version control
questions.explanation: A short AGENTS.md router (pointing to state file, task board, deeper rules, verification command) gets followed. A 3000-line manual gets ignored — the model loads it, cannot summarize the parts it needs, and fails on the same surfaces anyway.

questions.question: Why does state live in a file rather than in chat history?
options: Files are faster to read than chat history
Chat history is volatile — sessions die, conversations get trimmed. Files persist across sessions and agent swaps
Chat history has size limits that files do not
Files are easier for external tools to access
questions.explanation: Chat history is volatile: sessions die, conversations get trimmed, models change. The state file persists across sessions and survives agent swaps — the next session reads the file instead of replaying the chat.

questions.question: What is the 'nested AGENTS.md with nearest-wins precedence' pattern?
options: Multiple AGENTS.md files that conflict with each other
One AGENTS.md per subcomponent (e.g., OpenAI has 88 files); agents walk from working file toward root, concatenating each AGENTS.md found
AGENTS.md files that inherit from parent directories
A system where the most recent AGENTS.md overrides all others
questions.explanation: Nested AGENTS.md: one file per subcomponent, walking from the working file toward the root. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Copilot concatenate every AGENTS.md found on the path. Sub-directory files extend the root file.

questions.question: What anti-pattern causes agents to drop from 48.8% to 28% resolve rate according to ICLR 2026 AMBIG-SWE?
options: Using too many tools
Conflicting instructions (stacking them flat rather than numbering priorities)
Not having a state file
Having a task board with too many items
questions.explanation: AMBIG-SWE (ICLR 2026) found conflicting instructions silently drop agents from interactive to greedy mode (48.8% -> 28% resolve rate). Fix: number priorities instead of stacking them flat.

questions.question: What is a 'task on the board' schema in the minimal workbench?
options: A free-text description of what needs to be done
An entry with id, goal, status (todo/in_progress/done/blocked), owner (builder/reviewer/human), and acceptance criteria
A link to the relevant GitHub issue
A priority number and estimated time to complete
questions.explanation: A task on the board has: id, goal (one sentence the reviewer can verify), status (todo/in_progress/done/blocked), owner (builder, reviewer, or human), and acceptance criteria. The board is intentionally small — when it grows past a screen, you have a planning problem.
